nodes.rationale: Only the exact official file is accepted (SHA-256 pins loader, app, layout); in-browser revert later removed as unreliable, so validateStockPackage is unused.

nodes.label: Backup and restore
nodes.rationale: A damaged file is refused before writing; each object written as a save writes it so a cut-off restore never leaves half an object.

nodes.label: Bank Select (CC 0)
nodes.rationale: Reaches presets past the 128 Program Change range.

nodes.label: DX7 / SysEx patches (FM6 bank)
nodes.rationale: A project keeps the track's PTCH, not the patch: store an edited patch in the bank to keep it.

nodes.label: Favourites (FAV)
nodes.rationale: Favourites are an FM-1 setting, not part of a project or editor backup.

nodes.label: Install and update
nodes.rationale: Installer checks SHA-256 and the update loader checks CRC so a damaged package is refused before anything is written.

nodes.label: Offline editor and installable app
nodes.rationale: On Android use the app: Chrome on Android does not allow MIDI in a downloaded file.

nodes.label: SLOOP firmware
nodes.rationale: Free open-source GPL-3.0 firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1; projects from 2.7 load unchanged in 2.8 and vice versa for compatibility.

nodes.label: Going back to official firmware (M-UPGRADE)
nodes.rationale: 2.8 removed the in-browser return-to-stock because it was not reliable on every system; use M-UPGRADE (or Clipper's installer).

nodes.label: Arpeggiator
nodes.rationale: 2.7: while the arp runs, loading another sound keeps the arp; a sound's own unchanged arp goes with it.

nodes.label: Felucca (base firmware)
nodes.rationale: SLOOP is based on Felucca by Leo Kuroshita / Hugelton Instruments; many features are ported 'after Felucca' versions.

nodes.label: KBD HOLD (latch without arp)
nodes.rationale: Projects saved before 2.7 open with HOLD OFF when their arp is OFF, so nothing hangs by surprise.

nodes.label: MIDI
nodes.rationale: Bluetooth MIDI is not supported: SLOOP never switches the radio on.

nodes.label: MIDI channels (CH1-CH4)
nodes.rationale: Two tracks never share a channel: a taken channel moves on to the next free one.

nodes.label: MIDI IN / OTHER / OUT settings
nodes.rationale: Notes that came in are never sent back (no MIDI loop).

nodes.label: AUDIO CLK (audio sync click)
nodes.rationale: Drives Volca / Pocket Operator / LSDJ SYNC IN over a plain 3.5 mm cable, no MIDI-to-sync box; pulses only while playing so the slave does not creep.

nodes.label: Project (whole device state)
nodes.rationale: A project keeps the whole device state: sound and pattern of all four tracks, the selected track and the global settings. Projects 1-4 double as song sections A-D.

nodes.label: Backup Panel (Save / Restore)

nodes.label: Projects Panel (4 slots Load/Save)
nodes.rationale: Four project slots, each showing used/empty status with Load and Save buttons.

nodes.label: CHOP Editor Panel
nodes.rationale: Web editor section that slices a long sample (e.g. LONG20S, 20.00 s) into chops, shown as a dark high-contrast monochrome UI with a header summary of sound name, duration, chop count and kept count.

nodes.label: Per-Chop Length Trim
nodes.rationale: Selected-chop detail row (Chop 2 C#4) with keep toggle, length slider (0.92 s of 1.25 s), play preview and 'Up to the next marker' to extend length to the following chop marker.

nodes.label: Chop Waveform Strip
nodes.rationale: Horizontal waveform split into numbered columns at chop markers; selected chop highlighted in grey; unkept chops labelled with an em dash instead of a note.

nodes.label: Fit to Slot
nodes.rationale: Button (shown disabled/greyed) to trim kept chops so the result fits the device sample slot capacity.

nodes.label: Send to USR1/USR2/USR3 Slots
nodes.rationale: Uploads the kept chops as a user sample kit into one of three user slots on the device.

nodes.label: Chop-to-Note Chromatic Mapping
nodes.rationale: Kept chops are assigned consecutive chromatic notes starting at C4 (C4, C#4, D4, D#4...), skipping unkept chops, so each kept slice is playable from a key.

nodes.label: Chop Keep/Untick Selection
nodes.rationale: Per-chop checkboxes plus Keep all / Keep none; unticked chops go neither to the slot nor to the exported WAVs, letting a long recording be reduced to only the useful hits (16 chops, 8 kept).

nodes.rationale: Selectable drum kit for the drum track; 808 is shown.

nodes.label: Roll / Ratchet (x1-x4)

nodes.rationale: 16 drum sounds assigned to the 16 white keys from F3 to G5, so the keyboard plays the kit directly.

nodes.rationale: Web UI screenshot of the Sequencer tab with Track 4 (Drums) selected: pattern controls on top, kit/level/roll toolbar, and a 16-row x 16-step drum grid. Monochrome, dense, hardware-like layout.

nodes.label: Chord mode (one finger, one chord)
nodes.rationale: Every chord is built from the scale so it always fits the song; with SCALE CHR chords come from minor.

nodes.label: Drum MUTE mode (EDIT + black key)
nodes.rationale: Drum mutes are a performance tool, not part of the pattern: a loaded or new project starts with every sound playing.

nodes.label: EDIT layer (erase)
nodes.rationale: Erase is MPC-style: hold a key while playing to erase it from every step the playhead passes; all knob turns of one EDIT hold count as one undo.

nodes.label: Lock a layer open
nodes.rationale: Locking a layer frees both hands: one on the keys, one on the knobs.

nodes.label: Mute and solo (GLO + keys 1-8)
nodes.rationale: A muted track fades out in a few ms and its pattern runs on in time; several solos add up.

nodes.label: Tap and hold (two lives of a button)
nodes.norm_label: tap and hold (two lives of a button)
nodes.rationale: Every function button has two lives: tap opens pages, hold opens a layer; layer screen appears after 0.35 s (2.8.3) so a quick tap no longer flashes it.

nodes.label: VLEAD (voice leading)
nodes.rationale: Each chord voiced nearest the last so a progression moves smoothly instead of jumping.

nodes.norm_label: per-step sheet (oct+ held: slide, nudge, fill, move, copy, delete, ratchet)
nodes.rationale: 2.8.1: shown as a strip along the bottom so the piano roll stays visible; same sheet on the DRUMS grid.

nodes.label: Swing
nodes.rationale: Track swing adds to the global swing; triplet divisions are never swung.

nodes.label: Held notes and legato recording (POLY / MONO)
nodes.norm_label: held notes and legato recording (poly / mono)
nodes.rationale: 2.7-2.8.3: on POLY tracks held notes go on under new notes (up to 4 a step); on MONO/LEGATO a note over a held one records legato; screen hints MONO: SET VOICE POLY.

nodes.label: backupRestore()
nodes.rationale: Refuses before writing anything when the backup's projects are newer than the device reads; skips objects 8-11 a device lacks.

nodes.label: sloop-song file format
nodes.rationale: A song as one file: loop (object 0), sections A..D (2..5) and the order (36 bytes of settings at 48); the LIVE playlist is a list of these.

nodes.label: loudDb()
nodes.rationale: K-weighted (ITU-R BS.1770) loudest 100 ms window: a hit is heard by its loudest moment.

nodes.label: CHOP tool (slice a recording into keys)
nodes.norm_label: chop tool (slice a recording into keys)
nodes.rationale: TAP markers are placed on what the listener hears (output latency compensated) and snapped to the nearest hit.

nodes.label: Drum kit builder (16 pads -> USR slot, USR3+4 big kit)
nodes.norm_label: drum kit builder (16 pads -> usr slot, usr3+4 big kit)
nodes.rationale: A slot of the pair that gets no pad is erased so nothing old plays on a lane the kit leaves empty.

nodes.label: LOOP+TAIL sample loops (2.7)
nodes.rationale: A held loop goes round; on release the rest plays to the end, as the FM-1 plays it; loop points snap to zero crossings.

nodes.label: Samples page (USR1..USR4 slots, files or CHOP)
nodes.norm_label: samples page (usr1..usr4 slots, files or chop)

nodes.label: DRUM PREVIEW setting
nodes.rationale: OFF by default so picking a drum sound with a knob is silent, quiet for live.

nodes.label: DRUMS Sound page (per-sound TUNE / DECAY)
nodes.rationale: 2.8: TUNE also shapes brightness of tone-less sounds (hats, shakers, claps) that have no pitch to shift.

nodes.label: Four tracks (3 synth, 1 drum)
nodes.rationale: Track colour is shared with the knob of the same colour; white means what you touch, red means recording.

nodes.label: Drum kits
nodes.rationale: Every kit is level-matched; changing the kit never touches the pattern.

nodes.label: Drum voice allocation (6 voices, kick last)
nodes.norm_label: drum voice allocation (6 voices, kick last)
nodes.rationale: 2.8.3: a hit takes the voice of its own sound or the oldest voice, the kick last, so on a busy beat the kick no longer drops out.

nodes.label: KNOB ACCEL (knob acceleration)
nodes.rationale: After JIANT FM: slow turn fine-tunes, fast turn sweeps wider; LEVEL and PAN glide ~3 ms to avoid zipper.

nodes.label: The lights (button and key LEDs)
nodes.rationale: LIGHTS let labels be read in the dark (unreadable unlit on a black FM-1).

nodes.label: Master limiter
nodes.rationale: 2.6 look-ahead of one block (0.7 ms) so a loud hit is turned down before it reaches the soft clipper.

nodes.label: USB RATE
nodes.rationale: 44.1 KHZ only fixes phones that record the FM-1 distorted: the phone converts the rate itself.

nodes.label: 2ND CORE (dual-core audio)
nodes.rationale: Dual-core audio doubles CPU headroom; 2.8.3 checks every job and falls back to one core instead of crashing if the second core misreads under load.

nodes.norm_label: lvg() (live global param ids by label)

nodes.norm_label: lvp() (live track param ids by label)

nodes.rationale: Button actions go through LIVE (same firmware code as the buttons); notes as plain MIDI notes so no SysEx sits between a key and its sound; state read ~8x/s while shown.

nodes.label: PHASR insert effect

nodes.norm_label: midi learn screen (t1 dst send a cc)

nodes.norm_label: four-parameter page layout (top strip + 2x2 large values)
nodes.rationale: Consistent page design: four color-coded params in a top strip with mini bars, the same four shown large in a 2x2 grid so values are readable at a glance; colors map to the four encoder knobs.

nodes.norm_label: page footer (engine/preset name, page x/n, step ticks)

nodes.rationale: Each track has a fixed color reused in step grids, track badge in status bar, and parameter accents, aiding orientation on a small screen.

nodes.label: FM6 engine (6-op FM, DX7)

nodes.label: PHYS engine (physical models)
nodes.rationale: DaisySP and Rings models as Felucca 1.0 ported them.

nodes.label: SAMPLE engine (sampler)
nodes.rationale: SAMPLE sets are CC0 recordings coloured like a record through an old sampler.

nodes.label: Polyphony (voice pool)
nodes.rationale: 8-voice pool shared by synth tracks, drums have their own 6; oldest sounding voice is taken.

nodes.label: Sample loop modes (ONE SHOT, LOOP, LOOP+TAIL)
nodes.norm_label: sample loop modes (one shot, loop, loop+tail)
nodes.rationale: Loop points snap to the nearest zero crossing so the loop does not click; takes no extra memory.

nodes.label: The sound bank (153 factory sounds)
nodes.rationale: All factory sounds are level-matched; browsed by kind; changing a sound never changes key, chord mode, pattern or mix.

nodes.label: Greg Sullivan Wurlitzer EP200 samples (CC BY 3.0)
nodes.norm_label: greg sullivan wurlitzer ep200 samples (cc by 3.0)
nodes.rationale: Only non-CC0 source in the pack: credit to Greg Sullivan must be kept when sharing the samples themselves.

nodes.label: SLOOP Hip-Hop Pack (USR1..USR3 sounds)
nodes.rationale: Only free sources (CC0 plus one CC BY 3.0) so users own music made with it; no sound comes from a commercial record.

nodes.label: SAMPLE engine built-in sets source map
nodes.norm_label: sample engine built-in sets source map
nodes.rationale: Every built-in WAV is mapped to its exact upstream CC0 file so provenance is auditable.

nodes.label: KIT set (VCSL GM acoustic kit + hand percussion)
nodes.norm_label: kit set (vcsl gm acoustic kit + hand percussion)

nodes.label: PIANO set (VCSL Steinway B grand)
nodes.rationale: Until 2.1 the piano was VCSL's Upright Piano (Knight, DUSTY); replaced by the Steinway B grand and removed from the tree.

nodes.label: Track Engine Types (analog / digital / sample / drums)
nodes.norm_label: track engine types (analog / digital / sample / drums)
nodes.rationale: Engine type is shown as a dimmer suffix next to the track name, so each track's sound source (analog synth, digital synth, sampler, drum machine) is visible at a glance.

nodes.label: Track Row Layout
nodes.rationale: Each row: numbered colour tile on the left, track name plus engine type label, 16-step pattern strip with playhead marker underneath, and a horizontal level bar on the right. The selected track (2) has a filled bright tile and highlighted text.

nodes.label: Live Tracks Screen (screenshot)
nodes.rationale: 480x480 square device UI showing all four tracks at once for live performance: compact header, four colour-coded track rows each with a 16-step pattern and level meter, and a bottom row of four encoder-mapped parameters.

nodes.label: Encoder Parameter Row
nodes.rationale: Four knob widgets mapped to four physical encoders, each ring tinted with a track colour: swing 50%, level 81, steps 16, pan 0.

nodes.label: Header Bar (BPM / Transport / Record)
nodes.rationale: Large '101 bpm' tempo readout, play icon with bar.beat position '1.1', four-dot beat/bar indicator (first lit red), and global red 'rec' label plus red record dot indicating recording is active.

nodes.label: Playhead Marker
nodes.rationale: White underline below step 5 on every row, showing the shared current step position across all tracks.

nodes.label: 16-Step Pattern Strip
nodes.rationale: Active steps lit in the track colour, inactive steps dark grey; track 4 (drums) shows all 16 steps filled, track 3 shows none.

nodes.label: Per-Track Rec Arm Badge
nodes.rationale: Red 'rec' badge replaces part of the row on track 2, marking it as the record-armed track while the global recorder is running.

nodes.label: Per-Track Colour Coding
nodes.rationale: Each track gets a fixed colour (blue, green, olive, orange) reused for its number tile, step LEDs, and the matching encoder knob ring, tying on-screen parameters to tracks visually.

nodes.label: FM1_PORT / OUR_LOADER port filters
nodes.rationale: Only probe ports named like the FM-1 so other MIDI gear is never touched; a foreign loader (stock updater) is never written because it may lay the image out differently.

nodes.label: Black-key punch-in effects (KILL LOW/MID/HIGH, REWIND, OCT UP, FLANGER, AUTO-PAN, FREEZE, LOOP 8T, MONO, FADE OUT)
nodes.norm_label: black-key punch-in effects (kill low/mid/high, rewind, oct up, flanger, auto-pan, freeze, loop 8t, mono, fade out)

nodes.label: INSERT (per-track insert effect)
nodes.rationale: After Felucca 1.5; TYPE OFF or MIX 0 costs nothing.

nodes.label: Per-track filter
nodes.rationale: 2.8: the drum track has it too.

nodes.label: Punch-in effects (27)
nodes.rationale: Loops and gate are locked to the tempo and start on the grid; effect lets go cleanly on release.

nodes.label: REV THROW / ECHO THROW
nodes.rationale: Throws never change the song's REV values; nothing is saved or recorded.

nodes.label: TEXTURE (looping bed)
nodes.rationale: A looping bed (vinyl, tape, rain...) as the glue of lo-fi and ambient without taking a track; generated sources use no memory.

nodes.label: What's new in 2.8
nodes.rationale: Most 2.8 changes come from user comments and reports.

nodes.label: Recorded punch-in FX automation (2.8.5)
nodes.rationale: Pocket-operator style: effects played while REC is on are written into the loop and replay each pass; one effect at a time, 1/16 grid, up to four bars, stored with sections.

nodes.label: FX flush (FX + REC)
nodes.rationale: Pocket-operator FX 16 idea: a punch-in that removes effects; while recording it writes effects off to wipe recorded FX.

nodes.label: Parameter locks
nodes.rationale: Elektron-style per-step values, 24 per track; arp, key/scale/chord, voice mode and global pages are not lockable.

nodes.label: Punch-in fade (FX + SELECT)
nodes.rationale: 2.8: 0 (instant, anti-click only) to 15 (~0.37 s) so effects ease in and out instead of snapping.

nodes.rationale: Without WATCH: DUMP every 400 ms and two steps per round, since steps are not in DUMP.

nodes.norm_label: keep-alive ping and re-watch after gaps
nodes.rationale: After a long gap (hidden tab, flash write: Link.onGap) the watch may have ended: WATCH again and re-read what may have been missed.

nodes.rationale: Device pushes CHANGED / RELOAD / STEP_CHANGED; editor PINGs ~1/s so the watch (ends 3 s after last request) stays on, and DUMPs every 5 s as a safety net.

nodes.label: Self-caused RELOAD suppression
nodes.rationale: The device pushes RELOAD after loads the editor asked for; the editor re-reads anyway, so it skips that many RELOADs for 1.5 s.

nodes.label: SET coalescing (one in flight, one queued per key)
nodes.norm_label: set coalescing (one in flight, one queued per key)
nodes.rationale: SET as fast as the device answers: Link coalesces by key so a drag never builds a backlog; the user's value wins over pushes/polls while touched.
